findings.message: F1 (sources governance): specs/content/gict-300/sources/unit-05.md, ## Unverifiable sources, purdueOwl entry claims "the two-part habit it supports is the same habit the bound bourgeois2019 chapter 12 excerpt carries"; the bound excerpt (specs/content/gict-300/sources/texts/bourgeois2019.md, Chapter 12 section) contains no plagiarism or citation-habit material, so the corroboration cross-reference is inaccurate. The prose claim (topic-03.mdx, Avoiding plagiarism: Purdue frames the honest path as a two-part habit) is a modest paraphrase of standard guidance and the declaration otherwise honestly records the direct reading of 2026-09-23 under D-2026-0001. Repair: correct the declaration or bind a real corroborating excerpt; no prose change required.

F2 (attribution gap): docs/semester-1/gict-300/unit-05/topic-01.mdx, "Digital citizenship and its dimensions", teaches the respect/educate/protect dimensions taxonomy (seven of Ribble's nine elements) as "the commonly taught dimensions" without attribution; no bound source carries this taxonomy (digcomp2022 is scoped in sources/unit-05.md to the competence-side view; the commonsenseDC declaration covers its six topic areas only). Nothing is misattributed, but naming the framework or binding a source for it would strengthen the unit.

F3 (uncorroborated parenthetical): docs/semester-1/gict-300/unit-05/topic-03.mdx, "Intellectual property rights": the parenthetical "(though registration is needed to sue in some jurisdictions)" is hedged and factually correct but carried by no bound source and unattributed; the bound bourgeois2019 excerpt supports only automatic arrival on creation. Consider citing a source or dropping the parenthetical.

F4 (Bloom label): docs/semester-1/gict-300/unit-05/unit-assessment.mdx ERQ-2 is tagged (Evaluate) but the task - prepare a netiquette card with rules and one worked before-and-after example - demands Apply/Analyze; topic-02.mdx's own summative marking guide labels the same criterion (Analyse). The blueprint's Evaluate band is still genuinely satisfied by ERQ-5. Repair: relabel ERQ-2 as Analyse, or add an explicit evaluative demand to the item.

F5 (marking vocabulary): docs/semester-1/gict-300/unit-05/unit-assessment.mdx RRQ-10 model answer names "mosaic/patchwork plagiarism", a term not taught in topic-03 (which teaches "copying with small changes", synonym-swap and uncited paraphrase). The parenthetical "(structure kept, words swapped)" maps it to the unit's vocabulary, but the mark scheme's "1 for the form" should explicitly accept the unit's own phrasing so a correct answer is not marked down for vocabulary.

F6 (misconception placement): two of the four spec-listed misconceptions (specs/content/gict-300/content-spec.md ## Unit 5: "if it is on the internet, it is free to use" and "copyright applies only to books and music") are addressed only through the opening story, the Bourgeois copyright quote (which includes computer programs) and the teacher notes, rather than named-and-corrected in topic Explanation sections as the other two are.

F7 (link text): the three topics' Further reading lists (topic-01.mdx, topic-02.mdx, topic-03.mdx) use bare URLs as link text (3-4 per topic), reported as advisory by render-inspect; descriptive link text would improve screen-reader flow. Same pattern was left as advisory in the Unit 1 G3 run.

F8 (process note, no content change): the parent handoff stated the manifest was prepared at commit d7377ac, but the manifest's docs/semester-1/gict-300/course-overview.mdx digest binds HEAD 6361ad6 (commit 6361ad6 rewrote course-overview.mdx after d7377ac). All 97 input digests were recomputed with manifestFor() and verified twice against the current committed state (0 mismatches), and no unit-05 file changed after the authoring commit b33225f, so the reviewed subject is unambiguous; recording the discrepancy for the parent's traceability.
